bullets: Only 78.3 % of daylight intervals have both expected and actual data (minimum for a reliable gap: 90 %). Missing intervals were excluded, not treated as zero production.
paragraphs: Between 2026-05-01 and 2026-06-29 the plant delivered 76,067.4 MWh against an expected 78,491.2 MWh: a gap of 2,423.8 MWh (3.1 %). The comparison covers 78 % of daylight intervals; intervals without both values are left out, not filled.

In the assessment window (2026-06-23 to 2026-06-29), which describes the present state of the plant, the gap is 6.5 %. Combined standard uncertainty 2.05 % (k = 2 -> 4.11 %); materiality threshold 3 %.

Actual energy is SYNTHETIC (emulates MEASURED) (Synthetic stand-in for revenue-meter energy). Expected energy is SYNTHETIC (emulates MODELLED) (telemetry model; Synthetic stand-in for a weather-adjusted performance model).
sections.title: What the data show

bullets: Soiling of the module surface: moderate support. Soiling is plausible on indirect grounds only. A production gap, even a steadily growing one, does not prove soiling.

Operating temperature above the baseline's reference: not supported. The baseline already reflects the temperatures actually experienced, so heat cannot explain a gap against it - unless the temperature input itself is wrong.
Inverter or other equipment fault: not supported. Available equipment data show no anomaly. Estimated loss 157.0 MWh [SYNTHETIC (emulates MODELLED)].
Shading of part of the array: cannot be evaluated. Shading cannot be assessed from daily totals and no site observation is recorded.
Curtailment or downtime: cannot be evaluated. No outage interval was found; curtailment cannot be assessed without a log or sub-daily data.

Unclassified loss: moderate support. 6.3 % of expected energy is lost to causes that the available evidence does not identify. It must not be assigned to soiling by default. Estimated loss 2,266.8 MWh [SYNTHETIC (emulates MODELLED)].
